title: Probeable span proxy for loss-resilient replay
creator: Aisha Kaminski
description: Background: We observe intermittent span loss during high-ingest bursts when forwarding to a mix of legacy Jaeger collectors and Tempo backends. Current exporters do simple fanout or best-effort retries which either amplify load or drop spans silently. Goal: implement a lightweight, probeable span proxy that provides loss-resilient replay semantics, per-tenant delivery guarantees, and backend negotiation (compression/schema) without blocking ingest pipeline. The proxy will sit between the OTLP ingress and backend exporters and provide: 1) active health probing for backends with exponential backoff and queueing limits; 2) per-tenant soft-quotas and backpressure signals that surface to upstream rate limiters; 3) durable in-memory segments for short-term replay (bounded by memory and TTL) and optional soft-persist to S3 for very short outages; 4) downstream protocol negotiation hooks to translate problematic vendor envelopes (Jaeger v1/v2, Tempo ingestion) and strip incompatible tags; 5) observability endpoints for probe status, per-tenant pending queues, and replay success rates.
acceptance_criteria: Service implements health probes for each configured backend with configurable probe interval and failure threshold
Per-tenant pending queue metrics exposed (queued_spans, queue_size_bytes, oldest_span_age) in Prometheus format
Automatic short-term replay of queued spans to backends when they recover; replay success rates logged and visible in dashboard
When persistent failure occurs, spans are dropped with a deterministic reason code and tenant-scoped meter increments (no silent drops)
Proxy exposes a /negotiation endpoint used by runtime to map incoming envelopes to backend-acceptable formats (tests cover Jaeger v1->OTLP and OTLP->Tempo translation)
Integration E2E test: simulate transient backend outage and demonstrate no loss beyond configured TTL (integration job in CI passes)
Documentation updated: Confluence design doc, runbook for handling prolonged backend failures, and SDK guidance for respecting backpressure headers

2025-01-20 Aisha Kaminski: Design doc draft uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Probeable+Span+Proxy+-+Design. Key tradeoffs: memory-only vs persist-to-s3, chosen path is memory-first with optional S3 soft-persist behind a feature flag.
